question: How many Florida counties will be listed as reporting locally acquired dengue in 2026 in the FDOH Arbovirus Surveillance Report published on or around October 29, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Week 40 FDOH report: 368 cases from eight counties (Hillsborough, Pinellas, Miami-Dade, Orange, Pasco, Polk, Palm Beach, Broward). Brevard confirmed a locally acquired case on Oct 17, after Week 40, so the Week 41 report should say nine. The resolving report is Week 41 or Week 42, depending on publication lag (~5-7 days), so the remaining window is 1-2 weekly increments at a historical ~0.5 new counties/week, damped by late-season timing. No market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers. Mode 9, meaningful mass on 10-11, small tail to 12+.

Counties per news (Pravda Oct 17; natureworldnews Oct 15): Hillsborough (310 as of Wk40), Pinellas (37), Miami-Dade (9), Orange (5), Pasco (4), Polk (1), Palm Beach (1), Broward (1).

- Trajectory: Wk35 (dated Sept 10) six counties; Wk36 six; Wk37 six; Wk38 seven; Wk39 eight; Wk40 eight.
- Hoodline Oct 17, 2026: Brevard County confirmed one locally acquired dengue case; DOH-Brevard updated its advisory; widely described as the ninth county. It came after the Wk40 count of eight, so it is expected in the Wk41 report.
- Alerts (natureworldnews Oct 15): Hillsborough, Pinellas, Pasco, Miami-Dade, Orange, Duval, Alachua under alerts; 9 more counties under advisories. Duval and Alachua have alerts but are not listed with local cases.
- 2025 comparison: Wk41 2025 report listed 4 counties (Brevard 33, Hillsborough, Miami-Dade 14, Pasco). Late-season county additions in past years were slow.
- Publication lag: Wk35 (ends Sept 5) dated Sept 10; Wk37 dated Sept 28; Wk40 (ends Oct 10) was the latest posted as of Oct 19; the Wk41 PDF URL returned 404 on Oct 19. Wk42 (Oct 18-24) is expected ~Oct 29-31, so the resolving report is Wk41 or Wk42.

- Event window: the cumulative 2026 count as of the latest report on or before Oct 30, 2026; as of Oct 19, most of the window has elapsed and 1-2 weekly reports remain.

calls.reasoning: FDOH Week 40 lists 8 counties. Brevard confirmed a local case on Oct 16-17, so the status quo for Week 41/42 is 9. The resolving report is Week 42 (or Week 41 if Week 42 is late), leaving at most about one extra week of data. Counties have been added at roughly 0.5-1 per week, so a 10th county has a probability of about 0.3-0.35, with small tails at 11-12. The outbreak is still large (about 70 cases per week) and pool-only counties also count toward N. There is about a 5% downside to 8 from lag or reclassification (the Citrus precedent). No human market was found by any run.
calls.reconciliation: The three runs agree on the factual core: Week 40 lists 8 counties (Broward, Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, Orange, Palm Beach, Pasco, Pinellas, Polk), and Brevard confirmed a local case after Week 40. The minor factual dispute (whether the count reached 8 in Week 39 or Week 40) cannot be settled without web access, but it changes the implied rate only slightly. The unverified Hernando/Osceola/Seminole claim conflicts with the official list, so I disregarded it. The Citrus disappearance is a real but small downside risk. The remaining disagreement is pure judgment about tail mass at 10 or more. I put about 40% on 10 or more, given the large ongoing outbreak and that pool-only counties count, against limited remaining time. No web access on this run; no market found by any run.
